title: What certification do F-gas technicians need under the EU F-gas Regulation?
description: Regulation (EU) 2024/573 Article 10 explained: who must be certified, A1 to E certificate types, the 7 year refresher rule and the 2027 and 2029 deadlines.
shortAnswer: Under Article 10 of Regulation (EU) 2024/573, natural persons who install, service, repair, decommission, leak check or recover gas from stationary refrigeration, air conditioning, heat pumps, fire protection, switchgear and refrigerated transport units must hold a certificate. Certificates now cover natural refrigerants as well as F-gases. By 12 March 2027 Member States must require refresher training or re-evaluation at least every 7 years, and existing certificate holders must complete it by 12 March 2029.
keyTakeaways: Regulation (EU) 2024/573 entered into force on 11 March 2024 and repealed Regulation (EU) No 517/2014; Article 10 sets the certification and training duties for natural and legal persons.

Certification now extends to relevant alternatives to F-gases, including natural refrigerants, so technicians working on CO2, ammonia or hydrocarbon systems are in scope where the implementing rules say so.
Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2215 replaces the old Category I to IV certificates for stationary refrigeration, air conditioning and heat pumps with types A1, A2, B, C, D and E.

Article 10(9) requires refresher training or an evaluation at least every 7 years, with Member States applying the rule by 12 March 2027 and holders of 517/2014 certificates completing it by 12 March 2029.

Undertakings must check a contractor's certificates before assigning certified work (Article 10(12)), and only certified persons or undertakings employing them may buy F-gases for that work (Article 11(6)).
jurisdiction: European Union (all Member States; directly applicable regulation with EEA relevance)
regulator: European Commission (Directorate-General for Climate Action) under Regulation (EU) 2024/573, with certification and evaluation bodies designated by each Member State
appliesTo: Refrigeration, air conditioning and heat pump (RACHP) technicians
Technicians working on fire protection equipment, electrical switchgear and organic Rankine cycles
Technicians servicing refrigeration units on trucks, trailers, light-duty vehicles, intermodal containers and train wagons
Vehicle air conditioning technicians who need a training attestation
Contracting companies (legal persons) that install or service equipment for third parties

sections.heading: Who must be certified under Article 10 of Regulation (EU) 2024/573?

blocks.text: Any natural person who installs, maintains, services, repairs or decommissions the listed equipment, leak checks it, or recovers F-gases from it must hold a certificate. [Regulation (EU) 2024/573](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R0573) on fluorinated greenhouse gases was signed on 7 February 2024, entered into force on 11 March 2024, and is directly applicable in every Member State. It repealed Regulation (EU) No 517/2014.

Article 10(1) ties certification to equipment types listed in Article 5. The stationary list in Article 5(2) covers refrigeration equipment, air conditioning equipment, heat pumps, fire protection equipment, organic Rankine cycles and electrical switchgear. The mobile list in Article 5(3) covers refrigeration units of refrigerated trucks and trailers, and refrigeration units of refrigerated light-duty vehicles, intermodal containers (including reefers) and train wagons.

A lower tier applies to some activities. Article 10(1), second subparagraph, requires at least a **training attestation** (training completed, not an examined certificate) for servicing and repairing air conditioning in motor vehicles within Directive 2006/40/EC, for some recovery work, and for air conditioning and heat pumps in heavy duty vehicles, vans, non-road mobile machinery used in agriculture, mining and construction, trains, metros, trams and aircraft listed in Article 5(3)(c).

Article 10(2) separately requires **legal persons**, meaning companies, to be certified for installation, maintenance, servicing, repair or decommissioning of the equipment in Article 5(2)(a) to (e) and Article 5(3)(a) and (b). That makes F-gas compliance both an individual [competence](/glossary/evidence-of-competence) obligation and a company level one.

sections.heading: What must certification programs and training cover?

blocks.text: Article 10(5) sets six minimum subjects for certification programs and for training on practical skills and theoretical knowledge. A certificate may only be issued once the applicant has passed an evaluation process (Article 10(7)).

items: Recovery of the F-gases listed in Annex I and Section 1 of Annex II.
Safe handling of equipment of the type and size covered by the certificate.
Safe handling of equipment containing flammable or toxic gases, operating under high pressure, or involving other relevant risks.
Measures for improving or maintaining the energy efficiency of equipment during installation, maintenance or servicing.

blocks.text: Points (e) and (f) are new compared with the 2014 regime. They reflect the shift to flammable, toxic and high pressure natural refrigerants as Annex IV bans push the market away from high global warming potential gases, and they make energy efficiency a training outcome rather than an afterthought.

blocks.title: Design implication
blocks.text: A course that teaches F-gas handling but treats hydrocarbons, CO2 and ammonia as optional modules will not map cleanly to the Article 10(5) subjects. Each certificate type should have its own learning outcomes for flammability, toxicity and pressure hazards.

sections.heading: Which certificate types apply to refrigeration, air conditioning and heat pumps?

blocks.text: For stationary RACHP equipment, organic Rankine cycles and transport refrigeration units, [Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2215](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R2215) of 6 September 2024 sets six certificate types for natural persons and repeals Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/2067. Member States may issue separate or combined certificates, provided the activities covered are identified.

blocks.text: A certification body issues the certificate after the candidate passes a theoretical and a practical examination organized by an evaluation body, covering the skills and knowledge in Annex I of that regulation (Article 4). Certification bodies must be independent and impartial and must keep records allowing verification of each person's status for at least 5 years (Article 7(3)).

Two exemptions matter for workforce planning. Brazers, solderers and welders with a national qualification may work under the supervision of a certified person who takes full responsibility (Article 3(3)(a)). Trainees enrolled in a certification course may carry out certified activities under supervision for no more than 24 months in total (Article 3(4)).

sections.heading: Which implementing rules cover the other equipment types?

blocks.text: Article 10(8) required the Commission to set minimum requirements by implementing acts, and separate acts now exist for each equipment family. Each one repeals the corresponding act adopted under the earlier F-gas rules.

items: **Stationary RACHP, organic Rankine cycles and transport refrigeration units:** Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2215, repealing Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/2067.
**Recovery of F-gas based solvents:** Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/623 of 28 March 2025, repealing Regulation (EC) No 306/2008.
**Stationary fire protection equipment:** Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/625 of 28 March 2025, covering natural and legal persons and repealing Regulation (EC) No 304/2008.
**Stationary electrical switchgear:** Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/627 of 28 March 2025, repealing Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/2066.

**Mobile air conditioning and certain mobile equipment:** [Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1893](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32025R1893) of 17 September 2025, which sets training attestations M1 to M4 and repeals Regulation (EC) No 307/2008.

blocks.text: Under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1893, attestation M1 covers vehicle air conditioning and heat pump work with F-gases and hydrocarbons, M2 limits that to work with an automated recovery and charging station, M3 covers CO2 systems, and M4 covers recovery only. A 2024/2215 certificate may be treated as covering the attestation requirements for the relevant substances, and the same 24 month supervised trainee derogation applies.

Article 10(3) gives Member States one year after each implementing act enters into force to establish or adapt certification programs and make training available. National certification bodies, fees and course formats therefore differ, and an employer should confirm the national scheme in each country of operation.

sections.heading: Do existing F-gas certificates remain valid, and when is refresher training due?

blocks.text: Existing certificates and training attestations issued under Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 remain valid on their original conditions, but holders must now refresh them. Article 10(9) states that by 12 March 2027 Member States shall ensure that certified natural persons are required to participate in refresher training courses or complete an evaluation process "at least every 7 years".

For people certified under the old regulation, the first refresher or evaluation is due no later than 12 March 2029. Article 10 of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2215 then sets the level the refresher must reach for RACHP holders:

items: Category I and II holders under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/2067 may continue only if they update their knowledge and skills to the A1 and A2 level respectively.
Category III holders must update to the D certificate level.
Category IV holders must update to the E certificate level.

blocks.title: Status as at November 2026
blocks.text: The 12 March 2027 date is the deadline for Member States to have the 7 year refresher rule in national schemes, not a deadline for every technician. The individual deadline for holders of 517/2014 certificates is 12 March 2029. National authorities may set earlier or more detailed rules within those limits.

sections.heading: What must employers and contracting companies check?

blocks.text: Companies carry three verification duties that depend on training records. Under Article 10(12), an undertaking may only assign a certified activity to another undertaking after verifying that it holds the necessary certificates.

Article 11(6) restricts the purchase of F-gases for installation, servicing or repair to certified natural persons, or to undertakings employing people who hold the relevant certificate or training attestation, and sellers may only sell to them. Article 11(7) allows non-hermetically sealed equipment charged with F-gases to be sold to an end user only where there is evidence that installation will be carried out by an undertaking certified under Article 10.

For a legal person certificate under Article 6 of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2215, the company must employ certified natural persons in sufficient number to cover the expected volume of activities, and prove that they have the necessary tools and procedures. Headcount planning and the [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) are therefore part of keeping the company certificate.

blocks.text: Because a refresher is due at least every 7 years, an expiry tracker should hold two dates for each technician: any expiry printed on the certificate, and the latest permitted refresher date. The [guide to refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) covers how to schedule overlapping cycles.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models each certificate type as a set of defined knowledge points tied to the Article 10(5) subjects and the relevant implementing regulation's annex, so a refresher course can be checked against the A1, A2, D or E level a technician must reach. That makes it visible which skills a legacy Category I holder still lacks for natural refrigerants before the 2029 deadline.

faqs.q: Is a certificate under Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 still valid?
faqs.a: Yes. Article 10(9) of Regulation (EU) 2024/573 keeps existing certificates and training attestations valid on the conditions under which they were issued. Holders must still complete refresher training or an evaluation for the first time no later than 12 March 2029, and RACHP holders must update to the A1, A2, D or E level that matches their old category.

faqs.q: Do technicians working only with natural refrigerants need certification?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Article 10(1) extends certification to relevant alternatives, including natural refrigerants, where relevant. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2215 covers installation, repair, maintenance, servicing and decommissioning of RACHP equipment containing ammonia, CO2 or hydrocarbons, with certificate B for CO2 and C for ammonia, while A1 and A2 cover hydrocarbons alongside F-gases.

faqs.q: Is an F-gas certificate issued in one Member State valid in another?
faqs.a: Yes. Article 10(10) requires Member States to recognize certificates and training attestations issued in another Member State under Article 10. Article 9 of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2215 bars additional evaluation or disproportionate administrative requirements, although a Member State may ask for a translation into another official EU language.

faqs.q: Does the regulation apply to manufacturers working in their own factory?
faqs.a: Not for factory work. Article 2(3) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2215 states that it does not apply to any manufacturing activity undertaken at the site of the equipment manufacturer, and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1893 contains a similar exclusion for mobile equipment. Field installation and servicing by the same manufacturer's technicians are still covered.

factCheck.claim: Regulation (EU) 2024/573 signed 7 February 2024, entered into force 11 March 2024 (date of publication +20), repeals Regulation (EU) No 517/2014

Article 10(1) requires certification for installation, maintenance, servicing, repair, decommissioning, leak checks and recovery for equipment in Article 5(2)(a) to (f) and 5(3)(a) and (b), including relevant alternatives such as natural refrigerants; training attestation minimum for MAC under Directive 2006/40/EC and Article 5(3)(c) equipment
Article 10(5) lists six training subjects including safe handling of flammable or toxic gases and energy efficiency; Article 10(7) certificates conditional on passing an evaluation
Article 10(9): existing 517/2014 certificates remain valid; by 12 March 2027 Member States require refresher training or evaluation at least every 7 years; first time no later than 12 March 2029

Article 10(12) verification of subcontractor certificates; Article 11(6) purchase restriction; Article 11(7) sale of non-hermetically sealed equipment only with evidence of certified installer; Article 10(10) mutual recognition

Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2215 of 6 September 2024 sets certificate types A1, A2 (under 3 kg or 6 kg hermetically sealed), B (CO2), C (NH3), D (recovery) and E (leak checks without breaking circuit); 24 month supervised trainee derogation; certification body records 5 years; Category I/II to A1/A2, III to D, IV to E; excludes manufacturing at manufacturer site; repeals 2015/2067
Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1893 of 17 September 2025 sets training attestations M1 to M4 for mobile equipment, repeals Regulation (EC) No 307/2008, allows 2024/2215 certificates to count
Implementing Regulations (EU) 2025/623 (solvents), 2025/625 (fire protection) and 2025/627 (switchgear), all of 28 March 2025, repeal Regulations 306/2008, 304/2008 and 2015/2066 respectively
